entities.summary:
Marco d'Agrate was a prominent Italian sculptor of the Renaissance period, active mainly in Lombardy, Italy, from approximately 1530 to 1570. His most notable works include the marble sculptures for the altar and the bronze relief for the church of San Lorenzo in Milan. D'Agrate's artistic style was influenced by the classical ideals of ancient Greece and Rome, as well as the humanist movement of the time.

As a member of the Lombardy artistic community, d'Agrate collaborated with other notable artists, including Bernardino Campi and Francesco Primaticcio. His work also had a significant impact on the development of Renaissance sculpture, influencing future generations of artists such as Gian Lorenzo Bernini. The exact details of d'Agrate's life and artistic career are not well-documented, but his legacy as a skilled sculptor of the Renaissance period remains an important part of Italian art history.

In terms of his broader cultural significance, d'Agrate's work reflects the broader cultural and artistic trends of the Renaissance, including the revival of classical learning and the emergence of humanism. His sculptures continue to be celebrated for their beauty, craftsmanship, and historical importance.

One of the most striking aspects of d'Agrate's legacy is the enduring power of his work in the modern era. His sculptures can be seen in museums and galleries around the world, and his influence can be seen in the work of contemporary artists. Despite the passage of centuries, d'Agrate's art continues to captivate audiences and inspire new generations of artists and art lovers.
